recipes.title: Kimchi rib
recipes.description: Kimchi stew with pork ribs. Use all the kimchi brine and don't add too much water or it turns into jjigae - start with 2 cups and add more if it gets low. Whole-cabbage kimchi gives the traditional long strips; a bagged half-cabbage is the perfect portion. Can substitute spam, beef, or other meats.
ingredients: 1 bag whole-cabbage kimchi, with the brine
steps: Parboil the ribs to remove impurities.
In a big pot, add the kimchi with its juice and the gochugaru; bring to a boil.
Add the ribs and cook on low heat 3-4 hours.

recipes.title: RICE COOKER / IP KIMCHI ROLLED PORK BELLY
recipes.description: Kimchi-rolled pork belly, rice cooker or Instant Pot. Serves 2 adults + 2 kids.
ingredients: Sauce: 3 tbsp gochugaru (Korean red pepper powder)
Sauce: 1 tbsp gochujang (Korean red pepper paste)
steps: Cut the pork belly strips into 3-inch pieces.
Cut the base off the cabbage kimchi. Lay out each long leaf and roll a pork belly piece up in it, starting from the bottom.
Place the kimchi-rolled pork in the Instant Pot or rice cooker in a single layer.
Add the sauce and pour in water just to cover; add the onion and green onions.
Instant Pot: high pressure 30 minutes, then manual release. Rice cooker: sticky white rice setting (high pressure, ~30-35 minutes).
Serve with rice.

recipes.title: Shrimp paste pork jowl
recipes.description: Steamed shrimp-paste pork jowl. Future idea: put vermicelli noodles underneath to soak up the fat.
steps: Marinate the pork jowl in shrimp paste for 30 minutes (don't go past 1 hour or it gets too salty).
Steam for 9 minutes.

recipes.title: 東坡肉薯蓉
recipes.description: 東坡肉佐薯蓉 - Dongpo braised pork belly with mashed potato. Serves 4 (~994 kcal each: 22P / 9C / 93F).
steps: Pan-fry the pork belly in a dry hot pan until golden.
In the same pan, sauté the aromatics and add the sweetener; sauté until fragrant, then remove and set aside.
Add 1500ml water, return the pork, and add the soy sauce, thick soy sauce, rice wine, huadiao wine, and white pepper; bring to a boil then simmer on low ~90 minutes.
Cut the cooked pork into two portions, return to the pot, and simmer another 30-60 minutes.
Boil the potato until soft, then mash it.
Mix 2 tbsp of the mashed potato with the braising sauce until smooth; set aside.
Cut the daikon into pieces and pan-fry in sesame oil over medium-high until golden on both sides; remove.
Add the fried daikon into the braising sauce.
Blanch the choy sum.
Take 2 ladles of braising sauce and reduce over medium-high until thick.
Plate and serve.
